L'oncocitoma è una neoplasia renale beni:
Oncocytoma is a benign renal neoplasm (3-7% of solid masses). On CT it is often a well-defined, hypervascular mass, sometimes with a stellate central scar and with "segmental enhancement inversion" between phases. None of these signs is reliable, however: clear cell and chromophobe carcinoma can look the same, and central necrosis can mimic the scar.
For this reason a solid mass without fat should be considered potentially malignant; biopsy may suggest oncocytoma but does not always distinguish it from chromophobe. In elderly or frail patients, active surveillance is also discussed.
In this patient, histology after nephrectomy showed an oncocytoma.
La cicatrice centrale non basta per dire: A central scar is not enough to say oncocytoma: a solid renal mass without fat remains suspicious.
